## Results

In plain terms: this section reads off how strongly letter-sound knowledge tracks
each of the two outcomes — word reading and nonword decoding — from a **single joint
model**, and reports the difference between those two slopes. Because both slopes come
from one posterior (with a shared child intercept partialling the same stable-trait
latent), their difference is an **identified** contrast, not a product of two separate
fits.

Every slope is an **adjusted association**, latent general ability only partially proxied
by the shared child intercept — never a causal effect. The contrast is read as a
Campbell–Fiske convergent/discriminant argument (a pure-general-ability account gives no
reason for letter sounds to predict pure decoding *more* than mixed word reading), not as
identification of a causal decoding mechanism.

```{python}
# | echo: false
slopes = _csv("joint_mechanism_slopes.csv")
slopes
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | output: asis
if slopes is not None and len(slopes):
    _r = {str(row["term"]): row for _, row in slopes.iterrows()}
    _delta_key = next((k for k in _r if k.startswith("delta_ls_decoding")), None)
    if _delta_key is not None:
        d = _r[_delta_key]
        print(
            f"**Identified decoding-specificity contrast (Δ = β[N] − β[W]):** median "
            f"**{d['median']:+.2f} logit per SD** (89% credible interval "
            f"{d['lo']:+.2f} to {d['hi']:+.2f}); P(Δ > 0) = {d['prob_pos']:.3f}. "
            "This is a within-model deterministic — the true joint-posterior contrast, "
            "not the product-of-marginals sensitivity that two separate mechanism fits "
            "(`mech-096` / `mech-101`) can only bound."
        )
    _n, _w = _r.get("beta_mech[N]"), _r.get("beta_mech[W]")
    if _n is not None and _w is not None:
        print(
            f"\n\n**The two letter-sound slopes.** Nonword decoding: "
            f"{_n['median']:+.2f} (89% {_n['lo']:+.2f} to {_n['hi']:+.2f}); "
            f"word reading: {_w['median']:+.2f} ({_w['lo']:+.2f} to {_w['hi']:+.2f}). "
            "Both on one commensurate logit-per-SD-of-letter-sounds scale. A larger "
            "slope on pure decoding than on mixed word reading is the decoding-use "
            "signature."
        )
    print(
        "\n\n_How to read the table:_ `median` is the posterior median of each "
        "coefficient, `lo`/`hi` its 89% equal-tailed credible interval, and `prob_pos` "
        "the posterior probability it exceeds zero. `beta_mech[·]` are the per-outcome "
        "letter-sound slopes; `delta_ls_decoding` is their identified difference."
    )
```

### Posterior predictive checks (per outcome)

_Each outcome is checked on its own denominator_ (word reading over 79 items, nonword
decoding over 6) — the flattened bivariate likelihood never pools the two scales.
